preamble: Backing of the voiced alveolar stop [d] to velar [g] is rare. Its clearest case is East Baltic, where Proto-Balto-Slavic *d before *l became g in Lithuanian and Latvian. West Baltic Old Prussian addle and Proto-Slavic *edlь 'spruce' keep the dental, while Lithuanian eglė and Latvian egle have the velar. The voiceless counterpart *tl > kl went the same way in East Baltic.
